body.purpose: Default UI text: table cells, labels, descriptions.

label.purpose: Secondary metadata: sidebar subtitle, version tag, hidden-column labels.

mono.purpose: Raw technical content only: console/log output and Steam IDs.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single dominant action per view (Start, Create, New instance).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.375rem; height: 2rem; padding: 0 0.625rem; border-radius: var(--radius-lg); border: 1px solid transparent; background: var(--color-primary); color: var(--color-primary-foreground); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s ease, transform 0.1s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-primary), transparent 20%); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { border-color: var(--color-ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-ring), transparent 50%); outline: none; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.375rem; height: 1.75rem; padding: 0 0.625rem; border-radius: var(--radius-lg); border: 1px solid var(--color-border); background: var(--color-background); color: var(--color-foreground); font-size: 0.8rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--color-muted); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { border-color: var(--color-ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-ring), transparent 50%); outline: none; }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Quiet, low-opacity destructive treatment — never a solid red button.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.375rem; height: 2rem; padding: 0 0.625rem; border-radius: var(--radius-lg); border: 1px solid transparent; background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-destructive), transparent 90%); color: var(--color-destructive); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-destructive), transparent 80%); }

components.name: Default Badge
components.description: The 'true'/positive state, e.g. an instance that is running.
components.css: .ds-badge-default { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 1.25rem; padding: 0 0.5rem; border-radius: var(--radius-4xl); background: var(--color-primary); color: var(--color-primary-foreground); font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Secondary Badge
components.description: The neutral/informational state, e.g. a stopped instance or a plain count.
components.css: .ds-badge-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 1.25rem; padding: 0 0.5rem; border-radius: var(--radius-4xl); background: var(--color-secondary); color: var(--color-secondary-foreground); font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat surface, ring border instead of shadow, used for dashboard summaries and detail-page groupings.
components.html:
Dependency status
SteamCMD, game install, disk, network.
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1rem; border-radius: var(--radius-xl); background: var(--color-card); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-foreground), transparent 90%); padding: 1rem; font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--color-card-foreground); } .ds-card-title { font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.375; } .ds-card-body { color: var(--color-muted-foreground); }

components.name: Input
components.description: Text field used in forms (e.g. Create instance dialog).
components.css: .ds-input { height: 2rem; width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; border-radius: var(--radius-lg); border: 1px solid var(--color-input); background: transparent; padding: 0.25rem 0.625rem; font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--color-foreground); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--color-muted-foreground); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: var(--color-ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-ring), transparent 50%); outline: none; }

components.name: Checkbox
components.description: Independent multi-selection (e.g. picking instances to install a mod on); Switch stays the control for a single on/off setting.
components.css: .ds-checkbox { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 1rem; height: 1rem; border-radius: var(--radius-sm); border: 1px solid var(--color-input); background: var(--color-primary); color: var(--color-primary-foreground); } .ds-checkbox-icon { width: 0.75rem; height: 0.75rem; }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Item
components.description: Signature navigation pattern: hover and active share one visual treatment.
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; border-radius: var(--radius-md); padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-sidebar-foreground), transparent 30%); text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease; } .ds-nav-item:hover, .ds-nav-item--active { background: var(--color-sidebar-accent); color: var(--color-sidebar-accent-foreground); }

narrative.overview:
Odin's dashboard is a record-keeping tool, not a showcase. It exists so an admin running several Valheim servers for other people can see, at a glance, exactly what's true right now — which instances are up, who's connected, what a job is doing — and act on it without ceremony. The visual system reflects that: a near-monochrome charcoal-on-paper (and paper-on-charcoal in dark mode) surface, Geist Variable as the one typeface doing all the work, flat ring-bordered cards, and color spent nowhere except where it reports a fact the admin needs to notice. This is a deliberate, confirmed identity — not a placeholder waiting for a brand pass.

The mark (web/public/logo.png) — a painterly, dark-stone Odin figure with glowing cyan runes and molten amber accents — lives outside this system on purpose. It signs the product; it does not style it. The dashboard's restraint and the mark's illustrated intensity are two different registers by design, not an inconsistency to reconcile.
keyCharacteristics: Near-zero-chroma neutral surface (charcoal/paper), one typeface, one radius scale.
Color is reserved for status signals (ok / warning / critical) and never used decoratively.
Depth comes from a hairline ring border, never a shadow.
The illustrated brand mark is deliberately kept out of the UI's visual language.

rules.name: The Signal-Only Rule
rules.body: Alarm, Signal OK, and Signal Warn exist to report a fact about system state — never to decorate a button, a nav item, or routine content. An instance's own running/stopped state deliberately stays inside the neutral scale: "running" is the expected steady state, not an alert.

rules.name: The One Register Rule
rules.body: The logo's cyan/amber/painterly language never enters component color, icon style, or illustration. If a screen needs to feel more "alive," reach for typography, density, or motion — not the mark's palette.

rules.name: The One Typeface Rule
rules.body: Never introduce a second font family for emphasis or "personality" — weight and size carry that job, keeping the ledger feel consistent everywhere it's read.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth is a border and a background-color relationship, never box-shadow. A component that "needs to pop" gets a ring and a fill change, not elevation.

dos: Do keep color confined to the three signal roles (Alarm, Signal OK, Signal Warn) and use them only to report an actual state, never to decorate.
Do build hierarchy with size, weight, and tracking on the single Geist Variable family — never introduce a second typeface.
Do use a 1px Hairline ring plus a background-color step for anything that needs to read as "raised."
Do treat a routine instance's running state as the neutral default badge, not a colored one — reserve color for things that need attention.
Do keep the destructive button/badge treatment quiet (low-opacity fill on Alarm text), matching the system's overall restraint.
donts: Don't pull the logo's cyan/amber/painterly illustration style into any UI component, icon, or chrome element — the mark and the interface are deliberately different registers.
Don't drift toward a neon/gradient/"gaming rig" aesthetic anywhere in the dashboard, even though the product manages a game server.
Don't add box-shadow to any surface — depth is a border and fill relationship in this system, not elevation.
Don't color-code an instance's own running/stopped state (or any other expected, non-alerting state) — that dilutes the signal colors' meaning everywhere else.
